messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty triggered P1 -> Route53 health-check propagation anomalies detected for api.redwood-inference.com, elevated 5xx seen from EU regions. PD# PD-78912. Paging oncall-net. (link: https://pd.example/pd/PD-78912)

alex: I'm seeing lots of NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL from eu-west1 edge. Confirming with dig from 3 vantage points.

priya: yup, dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood-inference.com returns 10.2.3.4 sometimes, other times empty. traceroute shows spikes right after DNS lookup.

oncall-net: I'm paged, jumping in. Any recent Route53 changes? I didn't deploy anything.

caroline: No infra deploys. We did push a low-ttl change last week but shouldn't be this.

alex: sample dig output:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @1.1.1.1

# sometimes blank or NXDOMAIN
```

priya: logs from edge: "upstream_connect_error: connection reset by peer" correlated with DNS failures. Looks like some resolvers returning no answer causing our health-checks to failover.

oncall-net: Running dig +trace shows inconsistent NS responses from Route53 authoritative in eu-west zones.

caroline: Can someone test fallback to Cloudflare edge pool? We have a GeoDNS failover policy configured but it may not be kicking.

alex: Trying manual failover now -> updating traffic policy to prefer cloudflare-origin as healthy. Command:
```
# aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch file://failover.json
```

oncall-net: Applying now. Expect propagation delay ~30s-2m.

emma: Posting interim note on status page: "Investigating intermittent DNS resolution failures impacting EU customers" :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

jason: customer-reports coming in, main complaints are 502/504s for embeddings & generation. Escalating to CS.

caroline: After flipping to Cloudflare origin, edge error rate dropped ~80% in eu-west. Still seeing some residual 5xx for older resolvers due to TTL.

priya: TTL was 300s on the Route53 records — some caches may hold stale negative answers longer depending on resolver behavior.

oncall-net: Propose lowering TTL to 60 and re-apply routing policy, then monitor for two TTL cycles.

alex: Doing TTL change + re-triggering propagation. Command:
```
# aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood-inference.com","Type":"A","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.2.3.4"}]}}]}'
```

sre-bot: Automated check: EU error-rate pre-change: 14.7% -> post-failover: 3.1% (1m bins)

emma: Updated status: "Mitigated: Traffic routed to Cloudflare fallback; monitoring. Some customers may continue to see errors until DNS caches expire." :white_check_mark: 

oncall-net: Moving to P2 monitoring after sustained improvement but keeping PD open for 2 hours for follow-up. Handing off to next oncall (caroline) for the evening.

caroline: I have the handoff. Next steps: coordinate with AWS support to investigate Route53 authoritative latency, gather health-check logs, and prepare rollback plan. Also coordinate customers in EMEA with CS for any lingering issues.

jason: Notified affected customer list, will send targeted messages where error persisted.

alex: saving logs and dig/traceroute samples in the incident channel thread and in S3: s3://redwood-incidents/PD-78912/

incident-bot: Incident PD-78912 status changed -> Mitigated, severity -> P2. Assigned to caroline. Next update due in 45m.

caroline: Thanks — will update after AWS response. Keep alerting thresholds lowered in case of reappearance.
